{{distinguish2|the notable passive skill [[Corruption]]}} {{redirect|Corrupt|the prophecy|The Corrupt}} [[File:Corrupted item.jpg|thumb|A corrupted sword with a white socket]] '''Corrupted''' is a special [[modifier]]. Corrupted [[item]]s and [[strongbox]]es cannot be altered with most crafting methods, including restoration with an {{il|Imprint}}. There are limited ways to modify corrupted items. ==Sources of corrupted items== '''Warning''' - Some item corrupting sources have a chance to make an item lose all valuable modifiers. See related pages for more information on each corruption type. ===Corrupting uncorrupted items=== * A {{il|Vaal Orb}} can be used on a non-corrupted item, [[strongbox]], [[essence]] monolith, or [[Vaal side area]] (if {{psl|Lucid Dreams}} is allocated) will corrupt it may be otherwise change in the process. Items contained within a corrupted [[strongbox]] become corrupted as if a Vaal Orb was used on each of them. ** [[The Vaal Ruins]] in [[Act 2]] contains a Corruption Altar that lets you apply a single-use Vaal Orb effect on an item, once per character. * [[Beastcrafting]] has two map corruption crafts: # Corrupt a map to give it an implicit modifier. # Corrupt a Map Twice. This works the same way as the Lapidary Lens, picking two different map corruption outcomes (i.e. you cannot receive two corruption implicits, but you can create an 8-mod map with a corruption implicit). * Unique items that are obtained by corrupting another item are, of course, corrupted. These include {{il|Blood of Corruption}}, {{il|Malachai's Vision}} and certain [[List of unique jewels received by corruption|unique jewels]]. * Soul Cores dropped by [[Atziri, Queen of the Vaal]] (or legacy coin items from [[Mirage league]]) can be used on a level 20 [[skill gem]] to [[Imbue]] it, giving them an [[enchantment]] that grants the effects of a level 1 [[support gem]] to that skill and corrupting it. * A {{il|Coin of Desecration}} will corrupt a [[Restored Maraketh unique]], transform it back to its [[Afarud unique]] form and add a corrupted implicit to the item. * A {{il|Volatile Vaal Orb}} can be used on a unique item and it will either randomize the numerical values of its modifiers then apply a modifier magnitude multiplier of x0.78-1.22 rounded up or destroy the item. * [[Allflame crafting]] with {{il|Merrick's Ducat}} can craft a rare [[Abyss jewel]] to give it an additional explicit modifier and corrupts it. This can be done even if it has the maximum 4 modifiers. ===Other corruption sources=== The corrupted modifier may be found on items, strongboxes, monsters and areas. * Items can drop corrupted from various sources such as [[Vaal side area]]s, corrupted [[strongbox]]es, Corrupting [[Tempest]]s, {{il|Vaal Temple Map}}, {{il|Doryani's Machinarium}}, {{il|Vaults of Atziri}}, [[The Vaal Omnitect]], etc. Items that drop corrupted have a significantly higher rarity bonus for affixes, sockets, and links. * [[Vaal skill gem]]s are inherently corrupted, whether found in a [[Vaal Vessel]] or as a reward, or crafted using a Vaal Orb. * Various items bases including {{il|Thief's Trinket|Thief's Trinkets}}, {{il|Breach Ring|Breach Rings}}, legacy [[talisman]]s, and [[Leaguestones]] are inherently corrupted. * Certain unique items can only ever drop as corrupted. * Some [[divination card]] sets can be exchanged for corrupted items. * [[Vaal side area]]s are inherently corrupted. The {{psl|Lucid Dreams}} Atlas keystone passive makes them spawn uncorrupted, allowing you to use crafting currency on them. Entering an uncorrupted Vaal side area corrupts it. * At the [[Forgotten Shrine]] [[Atlas anomaly]], [[Ipaatiki, Vaal Priestess]] will allow you to take one double corrupted unique item from a random selection for free. ===List of divination cards granting corrupted items=== {{Drop enabled base item table |where=items.description LIKE "%Corrupted%" AND items.class_id="DivinationCard" |stack_size=1 |description=1 |responsive=1 }} ==Mechanics== ===Corruption outcomes=== For a detailed breakdown of various corruption outcomes by item class and specific special cases, see {{section link|Vaal Orb|Mechanics}}. ===Modifying corrupted items=== Corrupted items cannot be modified, with the following exceptions: * You can modify the socket colour, number, and links of a corrupted item using the [[Crafting Bench]] at your Hideout. It will cost additional {{il|Vaal Orb|Vaal Orbs}} equal to the number of currency items the recipe normally requires. * [[Beyond demon#Tainted Currency|Tainted currency]] items can be used on corrupted (but not uncorrupted) items to modify them with unpredictable results. * A {{il|Tainted Catalyst}} can be used to add a random percentage of a random [[catalyst]] [[quality]] to corrupted [[jewellery]]. * A {{il|Tainted Oil}} can be used to add an [[anointment]] to a corrupted ring, amulet, or Blight unique. * Certain unique items can be modified while corrupted. These items include {{il|Hands of the High Templar}} and {{il|Glimpse of Chaos}}. ** A [[vestigial unique item]] created from a Hands of the High Templar can be corrupted into a non-unique item while still keeping its {{c|mod|Can be modified while Corrupted}} implicit. * The [[Divine Font]] in an Eternal Labyrinth of Potential (Enriched Uber Lab w/ {{il|Dedication to the Goddess}}) offers crafting options that allows you to transform corrupted gems. * A [[Immortal Syndicate]] crafting bench will have a unique item and stacks of {{il|Djinn-Touched Vaal Orb|Djinn-Touched Vaal Orb}}, which can modify corrupted unique items. ====Twice Corrupted items==== Certain Tier 3 rooms in the [[Temple of Atzoatl]] can corrupt an already corrupted item a second time, turning it {{c|corrupted|Twice Corrupted}}. * The Altar of Corruption in [[Locus of Corruption]] (Tier 3 Corruption Chamber) can be used on a corrupted equipment to give the item all non-white sockets, add a second corrupted implicit mod, or destroy it completely. Double corrupting a normal {{il|Sacrificial Garb}} had a chance to transform it into a {{il|Shadowstitch}}.{{confirm}} * The Lapidary Lens in [[Doryani's Institute]] (Tier 3 Gemcutter's Workshop) can be used on a [[gem]] to add a second corruption outcome. It will not roll the same outcome twice (Ex. You can't gain a level 22 skill gem using this method). There is a chance this will destroy the gem instead. * The Dais of Corruption in [[Surveyor's Study]] and its upgraded versions can be used on multiple corrupted maps to add an additional explicit or implicit modifier, with a chance of destroying the map. ===Corrupted implicit modifiers{{anchor|Corrupted implicit modifiers}}=== {{main|List of item corrupted implicit modifiers}} Corrupted modifiers are implicit modifiers from a pool dependent on the item's [[List of item modifiers|item category]] and [[item level]]. Like other modifiers, it is possible for a corrupted implicit modifier to change an item's required level if the 80% of the implicit's item level requirement is higher than the item's default required level (e.g. a corrupted implicit modifier requiring Level 56 to roll will add a required Level of 44). Conversely, for most [[jewellery]] or [[quiver]]s, if a corrupted implicit's required level is lower than the item's default level, it can lower the default required level of the item (though it will still be restricted by the required level of explicit modifiers). Corrupted modifiers replace one (or two with double-corrupted) implicit modifier(s) from an item (if the item already has an implicit modifier(s)) and replace it with the corrupted modifier. {{il|Gilded Fossil|Gilded Fossils}} can be used to add the implicit modifier {{c|mod|Item sells for much more to vendors}} in addition to any existing implicit modifiers. Items that normally have 1 implicit modifier on them will have 2 implicit modifiers when crafted with a Gilded Fossil, and [[synthesised item]]s can gain up to 4 implicit modifiers this way. When corrupting these 2+ implicit items, there is a chance that the corrupted implicit will replace the otherwise useless Gilded Fossil implicit. Because the Gilded Fossil has no mechanical uses other than adding to the item's vendor price, adding it to an item will give it the potential to keep one or more useful implicit modifiers while corrupted. This is especially useful for items with sockets, such as {{il|Stygian Vise}} or {{il|Unset Ring}}. [[Synthesised item]]s or items with [[Eldritch implicit modifier]]s can also have more than one implicit modifier, and will only lose one random implicit modifier if corrupted via a {{il|Vaal Orb}}. Double corruption follows the same principles, though it replaces two implicit modifiers instead; in this case, the Gilded Fossil trick will only work on synthesised and eldritch items. ===Scourge modifiers=== {{Main|Blood Crucible}} In the [[Scourge league]], players could use the [[Blood Crucible]] to gather Corruption from slain Scourge monsters to corrupt an item (if not already corrupted) and add two Scourge modifiers, one positive and one negative, into an item. An item can be Scourged multiple times to add higher-tier Scourge mods. Unlike Vaal implicit modifiers, Scourge mods do not overwrite the item's implicits. Currently, there is no way to obtain items with Scourge mods outside of trading in [[permanent leagues]]. ==Video== {{#ev:youtube|5yhAuSU8cpc}} ==List of inherently corrupted unique items== {{Drop enabled unique item table |where=items.is_corrupted = true |large=1 |base_item=1 |level=1 |stat=1 }} ==List of unique items related to corrupted items== {{Drop enabled unique item table |where=items.stat_text LIKE "%drop Corrupted%" OR items.stat_text LIKE "%while Corrupted%" OR items.stat_text LIKE "%while \[\[Corrupted%" OR items.stat_text LIKE "%Corrupted item%" OR items.stat_text LIKE "%containing Corrupted%" OR items.stat_text LIKE "%are Corrupted%" OR items.name = "The Hungry Loop" OR items.name = "Angler's Plait" |large=1 |base_item=1 |level=1 |stat=1 }} ==List of item corrupted implicit modifiers== ===Equipment=== {{main|List of item corrupted implicit modifiers}} {{Query spawnable modifiers |where=mods.domain=1 AND mods.generation_type=5 AND mods.id LIKE "%V2%" |limit=1000 |stat_text=1 |spawn_weights=1 |level=1 |group=1 }} ===Jewels=== {{main|List of jewel corruption implicit modifiers}} {{:List of jewel corruption implicit modifiers}} ===Abyss jewels=== {{main|List of abyss jewel corruption implicit modifiers}} {{:List of abyss jewel corruption implicit modifiers}} ===Maps=== {{main|List of map corruption implicit modifiers}} {{:List of map corruption implicit modifiers}} ==Related Atlas passive skills== {{Query base passive skills |q_where= passive_skills.ID LIKE "%Atlas%" AND passive_skills.stat_text LIKE "%Corrupted%" }} ==Related passive skills== {{Query base passive skills |where=passive_skills.stat_text LIKE "%Corrupt%" AND passive_skills.stat_text NOT LIKE "%Corrupted Blood%" AND passive_skills.ID NOT LIKE "%atlas_settlers_2_6%" AND passive_skills.ID NOT LIKE "%UniqueItemsNode5%" OR passive_skills.stat_text LIKE "%Vaal Orb%" }} ==Achievements== These [[achievement]]s are related to corruption: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center;" |- !
